question.text: A spring whose unstrentches length is <math><mi>l</mi></math> has a force constant <math><mi>k</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The spring is cut into two pieces of unstretches lengths <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> where, <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><mi>n</mi></math> is an integer. The ratio <math><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mi> </mi></math> of the corresponding force constants, <math><msub><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> will be:

solution.text:
Spring constants of the spring will be inversely proportional to length.
k1k2=l2l1=1n
